findings.summary: The signature does not cover the cookie name, so a value signed for one cookie is accepted under any other cookie name.
With a secret, a cookie that is not in the signed format falls through to the unsigned return, so a client-set plain value is accepted as if it were signed.
A timedelta max_age is converted with .seconds, which drops the days, so a cookie set for whole days expires at once.

_lscmp() now uses hmac.compare_digest(), which raises TypeError for a str with non-ASCII characters; the signature part of a cookie is client-controlled (a quoted cookie may carry octal escapes such as \351), so a crafted cookie makes get_cookie() raise instead of returning the default.
